acceptanceCriteria: When one rendered top-level report section exceeds the Telegram character or line limit but contains complete level-three entries, the splitter divides it only between those entries, preserves exact source bytes and order, retains the existing semantic boundary, and keeps every emitted chunk within both limits.

A regression test covers an oversized AI-era reference-model section with multiple company entries and proves no entry is truncated or reordered; existing localized-heading, unknown-section, fenced-heading, and atomic-too-large behavior remains covered.

Focused splitter tests, repository formatting, clippy, and the full Rust test suite pass without changing report rendering, Telegram credentials, transport retry semantics, workflow scheduling, or archive policy.

The reviewed pull request is merged into main, the dedicated branch and worktree are removed, main is synchronized and clean, and the authorized non-dry-run Weekly Radar rerun for 2026-08-31 is verified from its workflow result and data-branch publication evidence.
goal: Restore production Weekly Radar delivery when a valid rendered report section exceeds the Telegram per-message limits, while preserving semantic boundaries, exact source content, and fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
intent: Repair the semantic message splitter after production evidence showed that valid rendered reports can contain sections exceeding the Telegram per-message limits.
outOfScope: Changing report rendering or report content limits
Splitting inside a complete level-three entry or silently truncating an entry that cannot fit
Unrelated Work Items or historical data artifacts

sources.reason: Repository governance requires a bounded Work Item, reviewed PR, merge, cleanup, and evidence-backed handoff.

Existing source-preserving, localized-heading, fail-closed, and size-boundary regression coverage.
